raw_response:
I'm 62 years old and I've farmed these 6 mu in Quzhou County my whole life. My wheat went in last October—improved Shimai variety, about 30 jin per mu—because that's what the seed shop always stocks and the grain station buys it without trouble. Right now it's greening up, and I need to topdress it with urea at jointing and run the pump three more times: at green-up, jointing, and heading. I'll also spray twice for weeds and aphids, and once for rust if the weather turns damp. After I cut the wheat around early June, I'll plant hybrid maize—probably Denghai 605—directly into the stubble without tilling. That saves diesel and time, and my nephew can drive the planter. For the maize I'll put down compound fertilizer at sowing and side-dress a little urea when the plants knee-high, then irrigate twice and spray for corn borer and weeds. I thought about planting a mu or two of cotton like some neighbors, but at my age all that pruning and bending hurts my back, and the maize harvester does the grain crops in a morning. I'll stick with what I know.
